correctness.rationale: For x=a and y=b-a, the normalized increments are independent Gaussians. Projection onto them gives the stated three inner products of the conditional mean basis; the independent residual adds only a deterministic trace to the conditional mean of Q. The residual after b is Brownian rather than a pinned bridge, which does not affect the projection argument. Isserlis and total variance give risk 1/3-2F, including duplicate and zero sites by dropping the redundant variable. Independent exact elimination reproduces the resultant and the linear relation y=-A/D. Sturm counting gives exactly three positive sextic roots, one per stated interval; on the first two brackets the signs of (A,D,-A-(1-x)D) are respectively (+,-,+) and (+,-,-), with zero counts for each sign polynomial. Only the first yields a feasible interior point. The witness 457/2916 exceeds 9/64 on both coordinate faces; its difference from the sloping-face polynomial is positive at zero and has no root on [0,1]. Compactness then forces the unique interior optimizer. Reproduced (a,b,risk)=(0.51844460651642214,0.85233448486089546,0.01965852971584853). The linear-area variance has cubic gap weights 1/12,1/12,1/3, giving (2/5,4/5); substitution gives quadratic risk 131/5625. value.rationale: Two exact Brownian values are a natural physically constrained information budget. The global certificate supplies a concrete nonlinear-goal benchmark including repeated and endpoint designs, and the 15.588% risk reduction against the linear-area optimum has a mathematical explanation: quadratic explained variance depends on the squared inner products of the projected modes, not only on gap-area variances.
